report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/eval/tasks.py chunk 1 of 2: docstring claims about task formats, provenance, and resolution verified against code; most kept, some uncheckable.
risks: AGENT_ENV_ROOT | medium | Claimed to be parents[2] of this file; if the file moves or is vendored, the root silently becomes wrong. | Verify actual path at runtime with a test.

resolve_task_repo | medium | Absolute-path branch checks os.path.isabs and Path(repo).exists(); a path that exists but is not a directory would be returned as-is, violating the 'repo root' contract. | Confirm with a test that a file path is rejected.

task_project_label | high | 'agent_env' comparison uses AGENT_ENV_ROOT, which is computed from __file__; if the file is symlinked or copied, the equality check may fail and the label would fall back to the raw repo string. | Confirm with a test using a symlinked path.

TASKS | medium | Inline comments claim labels were 'verified against the call graph' and 'ground truth follows the code', but this chunk cannot verify those claims; they may become stale as code evolves. | Cross-check with the referenced modules.

TASKS | low | The task set is hardcoded in this module; any change to the underlying code (e.g., rename of _reverse_edges) will silently break the labels without a test. | Add a test that validates the labels against the current code.

handoff.purpose: Define task formats, provenance, tier semantics, and the initial labelled task set for the distillation eval.

symbols.name: AGENT_ENV_ROOT
symbols.note: String path computed as parents[2] of this file's resolved path.

symbols.name: resolve_task_repo
symbols.note: Maps repo label to absolute root: agent_env, existing absolute path, registered project name, else raises ValueError.

symbols.name: CORRECTNESS_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple of keys ('fail_to_pass', 'pass_to_pass') that mark a task as correctness-format.

symbols.name: is_correctness_task
symbols.note: Returns True if task is a dict and contains any correctness key; presence-based, not truthiness.

symbols.name: task_project_label
symbols.note: Returns project bucket for --project filtering; <unknown> for missing repo, agent_env for special label, else raw repo value.

symbols.name: TASKS
symbols.note: List of task dicts; slice-recall format with must_include, all hand_reachable/primary in this chunk.

claims.text: Each task targets a real symbol/file in a small repo and records the symbols a *sufficient* distilled slice MUST carry to reason about that target.
claims.why: The claim about targets and symbols cannot be verified from this chunk alone; the actual targets are in TASKS but their 'realness' depends on external files.

claims.text: The labels below were picked by reading the code and VERIFIED reachable by running ``semantic_slice`` (see ``daedalus.eval.harness``); a label is only listed if a competent answer about the target genuinely needs it AND it is a real dependency or caller in the neighborhood.
claims.why: The verification via semantic_slice and the necessity of labels cannot be confirmed from this chunk; it depends on the harness and external code.

claims.text: For a symbol target the slice is 1-hop (the focus symbol's direct callees/callers), so we only label symbols reachable within that hop -- we do NOT claim transitive callees-of-callees are present when they are not.
claims.why: This describes slicer behaviour outside this chunk; cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Every task below is this provenance today.
``report.py`` says so on every render, and ``harness.run_tier1`` never blends it with the other provenances into one number.
claims.why: Behaviour of report.py and harness.run_tier1 is outside this chunk.

claims.text: Correctness tasks live in their own store (``correctness.DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH``) and never enter ``harness.all_tasks()``.
claims.why: References to correctness.DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH and harness.all_tasks() are outside this chunk.

claims.text: a correctness task carries no ``must_include``, so scoring one with ``harness._recall`` would return the vacuous 1.0
claims.why: The behaviour of harness._recall and the absence of must_include in correctness tasks cannot be verified here; no correctness tasks are defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``harness.eval_task_tier1``/``eval_task_arms`` refuse such a task loudly (an ERRORED row, which ``run_gate`` reports and fails on for a primary tier)
claims.why: Behaviour of harness.eval_task_tier1, eval_task_arms, and run_gate is outside this chunk.

claims.text: Deliberately keyed on the PRESENCE of the field, not on its truthiness: a task with ``"fail_to_pass": []`` is a correctness task with an empty (and therefore invalid, see ``correctness.validate_task``) test list, NOT a slice-recall task -- and it must never be handed to ``_recall``, which would score its absent ``must_include`` as a vacuous 1.0.
claims.why: The implementation uses `any(k in task for k in CORRECTNESS_KEYS)`, which checks key presence, not truthiness. An empty list still counts.

claims.text: A task with NO ``repo`` key labels as ``"<unknown>"`` rather than raising ``KeyError``.
claims.why: Uses `task.get("repo")` and returns "<unknown>" when repo is None; no KeyError is possible.

claims.text: That is not defensive padding: this function is called from ``harness._task_error_row``, i.e. on the REPORTING path for a task that is already known to be malformed, so a raise here turned "one bad task is reported as a degraded row" into "the whole eval run dies on it" -- the exact failure ``_task_error_row`` exists to prevent. Found by a test, not by reading.
claims.why: The claim about harness._task_error_row and the test that found it is outside this chunk.

claims.text: All Tier-1 labels verified reachable against the current slices -- which is exactly the circularity documented above.
claims.why: Verification against current slices is external to this chunk.

claims.text: Every task is "hand_reachable" / "primary" until an "independent_diff" or "temporal_churn" minter (see daedalus.eval.mint, a separate track) adds tasks with independent labels.
claims.why: All tasks in this chunk have label_provenance 'hand_reachable' and tier 'primary'.

claims.text: Updated when neighborhood expansion moved off the python-only dotted module map onto idx["import_edges"] (S2): ``_py_maps`` no longer exists, and its role -- supplying the lookup semantic_slice expands through -- is now ``_reverse_edges``. Ground truth follows the code; the symbol is still a real callee, verified against the call graph.
claims.why: The claim about code changes and call graph verification is outside this chunk.

claims.text: Updated by the HONEST DENOMINATOR change (slice.py::_whole_repo_tokens): the primary path is now idx["total_tokens"] (tokenizer-measured, carried through by build_index); total_chars // 4 survives only as the fallback for an index dict that predates the field. The label tested total_chars unconditionally and was never updated when the code it grades moved off that formula -- ground truth follows the code (see the comment above this task).
claims.why: The claim about slice.py and build_index behaviour is outside this chunk.

claims.text: Updated when the per-file pass was extracted into perfile.py and parallelized: build_index no longer calls extract_units/file_metrics/python_imports directly -- they moved behind _per_file_pass. These are its real current dependencies, verified against the call graph. The slicer was NOT the thing that changed; the labels were stale.
claims.why: The claim about code changes and call graph verification is outside this chunk.

claims.text: The task set is small + fast on purpose: agent_env (dogfood) + sunny_garden.
claims.why: All tasks in this chunk reference either 'agent_env' or 'sunny_garden'.

observations.what: resolve_task_repo's absolute-path branch checks os.path.isabs and Path(repo).exists() but does not verify it is a directory; a file path would be returned as a repo root.
task_project_label compares repo to AGENT_ENV_ROOT, which is derived from __file__; if the file is symlinked or copied, the comparison may fail and the label would fall back to the raw repo string.
The TASKS list is hardcoded with inline comments claiming verification against call graphs and code changes; these claims are uncheckable here and may become stale as the code evolves.
AGENT_ENV_ROOT is computed as parents[2] of this file; if the file is moved or vendored, the root will silently point to the wrong directory.
